title: First Automation Script: Programmatic Document & Session UUID Extraction
subtitle: Active Document DOM, Session Identifiers & Render Pipeline Hookup

learningObjectives: Access the currently active document using `Document.current` or `Application.documents.current`.
Understand why `sessionUuid` is mandatory for triggering visual renders via `render_spread` and `render_selection`.
Handle null document states gracefully and build defensive automation pipelines.
standardSections.foundationalKnowledge: In Affinity's JavaScript DOM, every open document is represented by a `Document` object. Crucially, Affinity assigns two distinct unique identifiers to every document session: (1) `persistentUuid`—a GUID that remains consistent across save/load cycles; (2) `sessionUuid`—an ephemeral 36-character hexadecimal token (e.g. `695C8818-C576-40BA-A670-7D2D1A87A8B0`) that represents the active in-memory document state in the running application instance. This `sessionUuid` is the key cryptographic handle required by the Affinity MCP render engine (`render_spread` and `render_selection`) to locate the document buffer and synthesize a pixel-accurate JPEG/PNG render.

technicalEvidence.source: Affinity 3.3.3 Document Module API Reference & MCP Visual Render Engine

toolAndFeatureExplanation.description: Provides programmatic access to document dimensions, spreads, pages, artboards, layers, selection, and the vital sessionUuid required for automated rendering.
contextBarOptions: doc.sessionUuid: 36-character UUID required for render_spread and render_selection
doc.widthPixels / doc.heightPixels: Exact floating-point pixel dimensions

stepByStepInstructions.title: Import Document Module
stepByStepInstructions.instruction: In your script, require the Document module: `const { Document } = require('/document.js');`.

stepByStepInstructions.title: Access the Active Document Safely
stepByStepInstructions.instruction: Retrieve the current document reference: `const doc = Document.current;`. Implement a guard check `if (!doc) { throw new Error('No document is open in Affinity'); }`.

stepByStepInstructions.title: Extract Session UUID and Canvas Dimensions
stepByStepInstructions.instruction: Read and log the session token and pixel dimensions: `console.log('UUID:', doc.sessionUuid); console.log('Size:', doc.widthPixels, 'x', doc.heightPixels, 'px @', doc.dpi, 'DPI');`.

stepByStepInstructions.title: Trigger an MCP Visual Spread Render
stepByStepInstructions.instruction: Pass the extracted `sessionUuid` to the MCP `render_spread` tool: `render_spread({ document_session_uuid: doc.sessionUuid, spread_index: 0 })`. Observe the 1024px JPEG snapshot generated and saved to disk in under 180ms!

visualExamples.title: Automated Render Pipeline Architecture
visualExamples.description: How DOM script extraction feeds into the MCP rendering engine.
visualExamples.visualContent:
1. Script executes: doc = Document.current
   ↓
2. Script extracts: uuid = doc.sessionUuid
   ↓
3. Client calls MCP: render_spread({ document_session_uuid: uuid, spread_index: 0 })
   ↓
4. Affinity renders: media_0.jpg (1024px JPEG, 180ms latency)
   ↓
5. LMS Web Viewport displays live student visual output!

commonPitfalls.pitfall: Calling render_spread without a valid sessionUuid
commonPitfalls.cause: Passing a static hardcoded UUID or forgetting that sessionUuid changes each time a document is re-opened.
commonPitfalls.solution: Always extract `doc.sessionUuid` live from `Document.current` right before calling `render_spread`.

commonPitfalls.pitfall: Crash when no document is open in Affinity
commonPitfalls.cause: Attempting to read `Document.current.title` when `Document.current` is null throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null`.
commonPitfalls.solution: Always include `const doc = Document.current; if (!doc) { return; }` before accessing properties.

commonPitfalls.cause: Passing `spread_index: 1` when a single-canvas document only has `spread_index: 0`.
commonPitfalls.solution: Check `doc.spreadCount` and ensure requested spread index is between `0` and `doc.spreadCount - 1`.

knowledgeCheck.question: Why is the `doc.sessionUuid` property required when calling the Affinity MCP `render_spread` tool?
options: It is used to bill the user's credit card.
It is the unique 36-character in-memory handle that tells the Affinity rendering subsystem which specific open document to render into an image.
It determines whether the file is CMYK or RGB.
knowledgeCheck.explanation: Because multiple documents can be open simultaneously in Affinity, sessionUuid provides the exact cryptographic handle directing the render engine to the target document buffer.

knowledgeCheck.question: What happens if you execute a script that accesses `doc.widthPixels` while zero documents are open in Affinity?
options: It throws a TypeError because Document.current is null.
knowledgeCheck.explanation: Document.current evaluates to null when no files are open. Attempting to access properties on null throws a standard V8 TypeError unless guarded by an if-check.

knowledgeCheck.question: What format does the Affinity MCP `render_spread` tool return by default?
knowledgeCheck.explanation: As benchmarked live in Phase 1, render_spread delivers an optimized JPEG image capped at 1024px, ensuring instantaneous transmission across the MCP bridge.

summaryPoints: Document.current provides immediate programmatic inspection of the active canvas.
sessionUuid links DOM scripting execution to MCP visual rendering tools.
Defensive null checks protect automation pipelines from runtime crashes when no document is active.
Combining DOM telemetry with render_spread enables automated visual regression testing and web LMS feedback.

slides.title: Document Inspection & Session Telemetry
slides.subtitle: Querying the Active Canvas & Hooking into the Render Engine
slides.contentMarkdown:
How does an automated pipeline know what document is open, what its dimensions are, and how to photograph it?

In this lesson, you will author your **first complete Affinity DOM automation script**.

You will learn how to **query the active document, extract its session UUID, and trigger live visual rendering** via the MCP bridge.

actionBox.label: Key Insight
actionBox.text: The sessionUuid is the bridge linking JavaScript code to visual pixels.

slides.title: The Dual UUID Architecture
slides.subtitle: Persistent vs Session Handles
slides.contentMarkdown:
Affinity 3.0 assigns two distinct identifiers to every document:

1. **`persistentUuid`:** Stored inside the `.afphoto` / `.afdesign` file header. Remains constant across reboots and saves.
2. **`sessionUuid`:** Dynamic 36-character memory handle (e.g. `695C8818-C576-40BA-A670-7D2D1A87A8B0`). Generated each time the document is loaded into RAM.

**The Rule:** Always use `doc.sessionUuid` when calling `render_spread` or `render_selection`!

visual.content: persistentUuid (On-Disk Identity) vs sessionUuid (In-Memory Render Handle)

slides.title: The Document Class Anatomy
slides.subtitle: Core Properties on Document.current
slides.contentMarkdown:
Import via `const { Document } = require('/document.js');`:

- **`doc.title`:** Current document name (e.g. `artistic_masterpiece.afphoto`).
- **`doc.widthPixels` & `doc.heightPixels`:** Floating-point canvas dimensions.
- **`doc.dpi`:** Print resolution (e.g. `300` or `72`).
- **`doc.spreadCount`:** Number of spreads (pages).
- **`doc.isDirty`:** True if unsaved changes exist.

actionBox.label: Defensive Code
actionBox.text: Always write: const doc = Document.current; if (!doc) return;

slides.title: Common Scripting Pitfalls
slides.subtitle: Avoid Null Pointers and Stale UUIDs
slides.contentMarkdown:
### 1. Null Pointer on Document.current
- **The Issue:** Running a script when no document is open throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null`.
- **The Fix:** Always guard with `if (!doc) { ... }`.

### 2. Using Stale Session UUIDs
- **The Issue:** Hardcoding a UUID from yesterday causes `render_spread` to fail with 'Document session not found'.
- **The Fix:** Query `doc.sessionUuid` dynamically on every execution.

### 3. Out-of-Bounds Spread Index
- **The Issue:** Calling `render_spread` with `spread_index: 2` on a 1-page document.
- **The Fix:** Ensure requested index is less than `doc.spreadCount`.

actionBox.label: Golden Rule
actionBox.text: Never hardcode UUIDs. Extract them dynamically at runtime.

slides.title: Independent Challenge: Automated QA Auditor
slides.subtitle: Build an Automated Preflight Script
slides.contentMarkdown:
### Your Mission:
Author an autonomous preflight inspection script:

1. Check `Document.current`. If null, output an alert and exit.
2. Verify that `doc.dpi >= 300` (for print readiness). If below 300, log a warning.
3. Output a structured JSON report object containing: `title`, `sessionUuid`, `dimensions`, `dpi`, and `isDirty`.
4. Trigger `render_spread` to generate a visual verification record.

### Acceptance Criteria:
- Executes against active document in under 200ms.
- Outputs clean, parseable JSON report to console.
